text:
emily: Heads up — noticed p95/p99 jump for /v1/generate starting ~09:02 UTC, looks like queueing/backpressure. Tenant: acme-inc. p95 ~200ms -> 1.1s, p99 ~450ms -> 2.6s :frowning:
raj: thanks. Any recent deploys?
emily: not in infra team, no deploys in last hour. Metrics: worker queue depth spiked, admission drop % up. Here's quick prometheus snippet:
```
avg(queue_depth{service="ingress",env="prod"}) by (tenant)
``` 
tom: can you paste a graph link? Also, which worker pool? gpu-small-1?
emily: pool=cpu-worker-3, tenant had burst of 600 rps -> concurrency limit hit, admission control started throttling. Logs show 'request admitted=false reason=concurrency_limit' for tenant acme-inc.
sasha: i've seen this when kv-cache coldstart + long sequences cause workers to be blocked. Any long prompts?
emily: customer sample shows 4 long requests with seq_len~8k tokens. Repro steps:
1) curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"model":"gpt-8k","prompt":"<long>"}' -H '"Authorization: Bearer ..."'
2) send 500 concurrent small requests while the above runs

raj: ok. Mitigation ideas: temporary increase tenant concurrency to 60, enable prefix caching for tenant, or route tenant to burst pool.
tom: i can bump concurrency for 30m. Doing now.
infra-bot: Updated acme-inc concurrency limit from 10 -> 40 by raj at 09:06 UTC. :white_check_mark:
emily: p95 dropped to 260ms within 2 mins, p99 still a bit high ~900ms. Need longer-term: auto-burst policy + warmup for long sequences.
sasha: file a config change: enable 'prefer-burst-pool' for customers with burst risk and add cooldown. Also add alert for sustained queue_depth > 50 per pool.
support-ops: I've emailed acme support with update and asked for repro sample. Also requesting sample prompt to test.
raj: follow-up actions: (1) rollout temporary concurrency bump for 1h, (2) create runbook entry, (3) add test to integ suite simulating long-sequence hotpath.
tom: created PR for runbook: https://github.com/redwood/runbooks/pull/412
emily: marking thread resolved for now but will monitor. :thumbsup:
